To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intracellular energy deprivation by AGAT deficiency activates AMPK and protects against metabolic syndrome only in the presence of leptin.
leptin and intracelular energy depletion act synergistically to activate AMPK and that this synergism is necessary for the protective effect of intracellular energy depletion on metabolic syndrome.
intracellular energy deprivation by AGAT deficiency results in AMPK activation, and that leptin sensitivity is a prerequisite for the beneficial effect of AMPK activation on glucose homeostasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of metabolic syndrome.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for metabolic syndrome, in which the combination of leptin with intracellular energy depletion may be a novel therapeutic approach.
the identification of a new target, the leptin receptor, for therapeutic intervention in the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMPK activation in muscle is leptin dependent and that leptin deficiency is a prerequisite for the development of metabolic syndrome in creatine-deficient animals.
AMPK activation is not only dependent on the energy status but also on the leptin status of the animal.
leptin is necessary for AMPK activation in AGAT-defective mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AMPK pathway is activated by energy depletion in skeletal muscle, which results in protection against metabolic syndrome in AGT-deficient mice.
the AMPK pathway can be a potential target for metabolic syndrome, but only if leptin is present.
the combination of intracellular energy depletion and leptin sensitivity is required to prevent the development of metabolic syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPK activation is not enough to improve metabolic syndrome, but it must be combined with leptin sensitivity.
AMPK activation by AICAR in combination with leptins can be a promising treatment for metabolic syndrome, but only in patients with preserved leptin sensitivity.
leptin is a key factor in the regulation of AMPK activity.
